config.title: Generic List<T>

intro.title: Generic List<T>
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a reusable Vue component that displays a list of items of any type, such as a list of names, numbers, or products. You will learn about Vue's built-in reactivity system and how to use props to pass data into components. The core programming concept is generics, which allows your component to work with different data types without rewriting code. You'll use Vue's template syntax to render the list and practice defining props with type validation to make your component flexible and type-safe.
intro.usecase: Generic List<T> patterns appear throughout modern web applications where developers need to handle collections of data with consistent type safety. In Vue applications, you'll use these patterns when building data tables in admin dashboards, product lists in e-commerce interfaces, or user selection components in forms. This approach ensures your components work reliably with different data types—whether displaying customer records, inventory items, or notification messages—while maintaining clean, reusable code. Mastering generics helps you create flexible list components that adapt to various data structures without sacrificing type checking or code clarity.

objectives: Implement a generic Vue component that accepts a type parameter for list items.
Initialize a reactive array state to store a list of items of a specified type.
Configure the component to render a list of items using the v-for directive.
Apply type safety by defining and using a prop interface for the list data.
Manipulate the list state by adding and removing items through component methods.
Bind user input to update the list with new items of the correct type.
Control the rendering of list items conditionally based on the array's length.

steps.title: Import Vue and ref from 'vue'
steps.instruction: In the script section, import Vue and the ref function from the 'vue' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with curly braces to import multiple named exports from 'vue'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing multiple named exports
import { ref, computed } from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: The Vue framework and ref function are imported and ready to use for reactive state.
successCriteria: Vue and ref are imported from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're importing both Vue and ref from the 'vue' package using the correct syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: import both Vue and ref from the 'vue' package using the import statement.

steps.title: Create a Vue component with a generic list function
steps.instruction: Create a functional Vue component named GenericListDemo that returns an empty template wrapper.
steps.hint: Define a component function that returns a template with a root div element.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Vue component named GenericListDemo is defined with an empty template wrapper.
successCriteria: The component is named GenericListDemo and returns a template with a root div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your component is named GenericListDemo and returns a template with a root div element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Check that you've named it GenericListDemo and it returns a template with a root div element.

steps.title: Initialize state with a numbers array using ref
steps.instruction: Inside your component, create a reactive state variable named 'numbers' using ref and initialize it with an array of numbers like [1, 2, 3, 4, 5].
steps.hint: Use the ref function you imported earlier to create a reactive reference to an array of numbers.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating reactive state with an array
const items = ref(['apple', 'banana', 'cherry'])
steps.expectedOutcome: A reactive 'numbers' state variable will be created with an initial array of numbers.
successCriteria: The component contains a 'numbers' variable created with ref() and initialized with an array of numbers.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using ref() and initializing it with an array of numbers.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try creating a reactive state variable named 'numbers' using ref() with an array of numbers as the initial value.

steps.title: Initialize state with a strings array using ref
steps.instruction: Inside your component, create a second reactive state variable named 'strings' using ref, initialized with an array of strings like ['apple', 'banana', 'cherry'].
steps.hint: Use the ref function to create another reactive reference, similar to how you created the numbers array in the previous step.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: another reactive state variable
const colors = ref(['red', 'green', 'blue'])
steps.expectedOutcome: Your component will have two reactive state variables: 'numbers' and 'strings', both initialized with arrays.
successCriteria: A reactive state variable named 'strings' is created using ref and initialized with an array of strings.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using ref to create a reactive variable named 'strings' with an array of strings.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create a reactive state variable named 'strings' using ref, initialized with an array of strings like ['apple', 'banana', 'cherry'].

steps.title: Define a handler to call the generic function with numbers
steps.instruction: In your component, define a method named 'processNumbers' that calls the generic list function with the numbers array and returns the result.
steps.hint: Create a method that uses the generic function you defined earlier, passing the numbers array as an argument.
steps.expectedOutcome: A method named 'processNumbers' is defined that calls the generic list function with the numbers array.
successCriteria: The component contains a 'processNumbers' method that returns the result of calling the generic list function with the numbers array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your method is named 'processNumbers' and it calls the generic list function with the numbers array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The method isn't quite right. Check that you've named it 'processNumbers' and that it properly calls the generic list function with the numbers array.

steps.title: Define a handler to call the generic function with strings
steps.instruction: Inside your component, define a method named 'handleStrings' that calls the generic list function with the strings state and returns the result.
steps.hint: Create a function that uses your generic function with the strings array state.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a 'handleStrings' method that processes the strings array using the generic function.
successCriteria: A 'handleStrings' method is defined that calls the generic function with the strings state and returns the result.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your handler calls the generic function with the strings state and returns the result.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handler isn't defined correctly. Create a method named 'handleStrings' that processes the strings array.

steps.title: Return the template structure with two sections
steps.instruction: In the template section, return a div with two child div elements: one with id 'numbers-section' and one with id 'strings-section'.
steps.hint: Use the template section to define the HTML structure. Create a main div wrapper with two div children inside.
steps.analogousExample: // Similar: template with two sections
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now has a structure with two empty div sections ready to display numbers and strings.
successCriteria: The template contains a main div with two child div elements having ids 'numbers-section' and 'strings-section'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have exactly two div elements inside the main div, each with the correct id attributes.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template structure doesn't match the requirement. Please create a main div with two child div elements having ids 'numbers-section' and 'strings-section'.

steps.title: Display the numbers array and its length
steps.instruction: Inside the #numbers-section div, add a paragraph that displays the numbers array and its length using the numbers handler.
steps.hint: Use the numbers array from the ref and call the numbers handler to get the length. Display both values in a single paragraph.
steps.analogousExample:
// Displaying array and its length

Array: [1, 2, 3], Length: 3
steps.expectedOutcome: The numbers section should show the numbers array and its calculated length in a paragraph element.
successCriteria: A paragraph element is added inside #numbers-section that displays both the numbers array and its length.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a paragraph, but make sure it shows both the numbers array and its length.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph isn't displaying the numbers array and its length correctly. Check that you're using the numbers array and calling the numbers handler.

steps.title: Display the strings array and its length
steps.instruction: Inside the second div (id='strings-section'), add a paragraph that displays the strings array and its length using the strings handler.
steps.hint:
Use the same pattern as the numbers section: create a

element with text that shows the array and its length.
steps.analogousExample:
// Displaying array and length in Vue template

Strings: {{ stringsArray }}, Length: {{ stringsArray.length }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The strings section will show the strings array and its length in a paragraph.
successCriteria: A paragraph element exists inside the strings-section div that displays the strings array and its length.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a paragraph, but make sure it shows both the strings array and its length.
steps.feedbackWrong: The strings section should contain a paragraph displaying the strings array and its length.

steps.title: Add a button to add a new number and wire its click
steps.instruction: Add a button inside the numbers section that, when clicked, pushes a new number to the numbers array. Wire its click event to a handler.
steps.hint: Use the @click directive to call a handler that modifies the numbersArray reactive state.
steps.expectedOutcome: A button appears in the numbers section that, when clicked, adds a new number to the array and updates the displayed list.
successCriteria: A button with a click handler is added to the numbers section, and the handler modifies the numbersArray.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but the click handler might be missing or not modifying the numbersArray correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button or its click handler is not properly implemented. Review how to add event handlers in Vue.
